title: Python recall gap: raise incoming-call recall of the native Python indexer, designed from Python semantics (DEC-303 (a19))
description: The S8 gate run (GCLI-83, 2026-11-25) FAILED on both repositories: click 68/80 = 0.8500 (Wilson lower 0.7559), requests 57/65 = 0.8769 (Wilson lower 0.7755), against recall >= 0.9 with Wilson lower >= 0.8 (DEC-303 (a2), (a5)); precision passed. DEC-303 (a19) (ODOC-640): the thresholds stand; the click and requests samples are spent as held-out evidence and are REFUSED as development data; this task is designed from Python's semantics under (a11), never from the per-site misses in those samples, and glyph-cli does not open the per-site misses of the click or requests ground truth to design it. Any later claim that glyph passes needs a FRESH blind sample drawn and classified before any analyzer run under the (a2) and (a3) conventions. The 0.1.0 tag and publish stay HELD pending the operator's release-scope question (dec-13m90z3).

acceptanceCriteria.text: a design note derives the unresolved-call classes from Python semantics (binding, descriptors, inheritance, imports) without reference to the click or requests per-site misses, and says so
each analyzer change is proven by fixtures written from the language semantics, tests both ways
no use of test/python-gate or test/python-lsp-measurement ground truth, per-site misses or the scorer in design or tuning
a fresh blind sample is drawn and classified before any analyzer run, under the (a2) and (a3) conventions, before any pass claim
